questions.stem: Regarding System feedback: a designer reviewing a community theater's playbill notices that a form gives no confirmation at all after submission. Which core usability principle is being ignored?

options.text: Recognition rather than recall as a memory aid
options.misconception: names a different usability goal than the one at issue

options.text: Aesthetic minimalism pursued at any possible cost
options.misconception: mistakes unhelpful silence for genuinely minimal design

options.text: Visibility of system status through clear and timely feedback
Error prevention considered in complete isolation
options.misconception: narrows the focus when feedback is the actual problem

questions.explanation: Users need to know what happened after they take an action. Without a confirmation or visible status change, a submitted form leaves them uncertain, so clear feedback about system status is essential to a usable interface.
questions.hint: How does a user ever know that their action actually succeeded?

questions.subject: GRAPHIC_DESIGN
questions.learningObjective: evaluate interface consistency in a design critique
questions.stem: On Interface consistency: a designer reviewing a museum exhibition poster notices that the very same action is labeled differently on two screens. Which usability goal is primarily affected?

options.text: Flexibility, because having more labels creates more options
options.misconception: confuses variety in wording with genuine consistency

options.text: Consistency, because matching labels reduce the need to relearn
Aesthetics, because words affect beauty and nothing more
options.misconception: dismisses the important functional role of labels

options.text: Error recovery, because clearer labels fix past mistakes

questions.explanation: Consistency lets users apply what they learned in one place to another. When the same action has different labels, people must relearn it and are more likely to hesitate, so consistent wording directly supports efficiency.
questions.hint: What do users rely on when they move between different screens?
